messages:
Noah Patel: Quick question  I just got married abroad and my spouse will move to the US next month. Can I add them to my medical and dental mid-year? What documents will HR/insurer need?

Riley (People Ops): Congrats! Short version: marriage is usually a QLE, but foreign docs often need extra verification. We'll need the marriage certificate; if it's not in English, the carrier will want a certified translation and sometimes an apostille.

Noah Patel: They don't have a SSN yet (applied, pending). Will that block enrollment?

Marta (Benefits): SSN pending is okay for initial submission in many cases. We can enroll spouse provisionally using name+DOB+passport number, and then update SSN later when it arrives. Carrier rules vary; some require SSN within 30-60 days. We'll note that on the case.

Noah Patel: What about the certificate type? The marriage was registered with the municipality, we have a copy but it's a regional format.

Riley (People Ops): Send the original scanned certificate. If the carrier rejects the format, they usually ask for a certified translation and apostille/legalization. We can escalate to the carrier rep if they insist on additional authentication.

Noah Patel: Any tax or payroll side effects if I add a non-U.S. spouse? Heard about imputed income for domestic partners.

Marta (Benefits): Important: if your spouse is not a tax dependent or doesn't have US tax residency, employer-covered spousal premiums may be considered taxable imputed income. If you enroll them as a spouse on the plan and they're not your tax dependent, payroll may treat the premium value as taxable. We recommend talking to payroll/your tax advisor. People Ops can flag payroll to apply imputed income rules when we submit the change.

Noah Patel: How do I submit docs? Email or portal? Any subject line?

Riley (People Ops): Email benefits@redwood.com with subject: "QLE - Add spouse (marriage abroad)". Attach: 1) Scanned marriage certificate, 2) Translated copy (if not English) or note if translation pending, 3) Spouse passport/photo ID, 4) Proof of name/DOB for your plan form (if different), 5) Expected US arrival date and SSN pending note. We'll open a carrier case and reply with any carrier-specific asks.

Noah Patel: Timeline  if they arrive next month can coverage start at arrival date?

Marta (Benefits): Carrier effective dates depend. Often coverage can be effective on the date of the QLE (marriage date) or the date you request during the QLE window. If you request the coverage to start on arrival date, we can ask carrier to align, otherwise some carriers will allow retroactive effective date to the marriage date. Submit within 30-60 days of the marriage to preserve retroactive options.

Noah Patel: What if the carrier says they need an apostille and I don't have time before arrival?

Riley (People Ops): We'll submit what you have and document the apostille as "in progress." Many carriers accept provisional enrollment pending receipt of outstanding legalizations, but some do not. If the carrier denies, you can still enroll during open enrollment; also you can add once the apostille is obtained as a QLE if within the allowed window.

Noah Patel: Ok thanks. Anything I'm missing re: dependents? Our daughter is with me already on the plan; do I need to re-submit anything for her?

Marta (Benefits): If she's already enrolled, no need to re-submit. If you want to add the spouse as additional dependent for dental/vision only, state that in the email so we handle each plan separately. Also note provider networks: if your spouse prefers certain providers, check plan network coverage before adding.

people-ops-bot: Reminder: QLE docs should be submitted within carrier windows (usually 30-60 days). Open enrollment dates: Nov 1-15. Changes take effect Jan 1 unless carrier specifies otherwise.

Noah Patel: Sending docs now, appreciate the guidance :pray:
